To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystallization of a Clonorchis sinus 26 kDa GST and its fusion protein with peptides of different length has been achieved.

crystallization of Clonochis sinensis 24 kDa glutathion S-transferase (CSGST) and its N-terminus fused with peptides of different length can be achieved by using polyethylene glycerol monomethyleter 550 (PEG 550) as a precipitant and that crystals of the fusion proteins are isomorphous with those of the native protein, suggesting that the system may be generally applicable.
the crystallization of CsGST/extended peptide fusion proteins is a useful system to obtain crystals of the small peptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crystallization of a Clonorchis 26 kDa GST and two of its fusion proteins containing N-terminal-extended peptide sequences.
the crystallization of CsGST and its N-terminally extended fusion proteins.
the crystallization of a Clonorchis GST fusion protein, and the results obtained may provide useful information for the crystallization of small peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of a crystallized CsGST fusion protein, and the results obtained in this study will be useful in the crystallization and structure determination of CsGST.

the crystallization conditions of CsGST and its fusion proteins are very similar, indicating that the crystal structure of CsGST can be determined by molecular-replacement methods using the structure of the fusion protein as a search model.
the crystallization of CsGST/ peptide fusion proteins is a useful method for crystallizing small peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a crystallization system for CsGST and its fusion proteins and that we have successfully incorporated a peptide of different length into a CsGST crystal.

the crystallization of the fusion proteins containing the peptides of different lengths can provide the crystals of peptides with high quality, which may be useful for structural studies of the peptides by NMR and X-ray diffraction methods.
a fusion protein of a GST and a peptide of 48 amino acids is crystallizable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallization of a protein fused to a peptide is not necessarily affected by the length of the peptide.
it is possible to crystallize peptides of various lengths fused to a crystallizable protein, and that the fusion proteins may crystallize with the peptides incorporated into the crystal lattice.
the crystallization of the fusion protein may be a general method for crystallizing small peptides.
